summary: Two law firms were fined $31,000 after filing a court brief with fake and inaccurate legal citations produced with AI tools. The judge found the AI use was not disclosed and that a revised brief still contained made-up material.
technical_summary: Large language models were used to draft a legal research outline that included nonexistent cases and invented quotations. The text was passed to a second firm and filed without cite-checking. A resubmitted brief removed two flagged citations but retained other AI-generated errors.

technology.quote: ultimately made clear that the source of this problem was the inappropriate use of, and reliance on, AI tools

failure_mode.quote: At least two of the authorities cited do not exist at all.

harm_type.quote: approximately nine of the 27 legal citations in the ten-page brief were incorrect in some way

notes: Errors were caught by the court; harm was sanctions and wasted court time.

summary: A Black man in Georgia was arrested and jailed for six days over thefts in Louisiana, a state he had never visited. A facial recognition match was the only basis, and police documents did not mention it. The parish later paid a $200,000 settlement.
technical_summary: Police ran surveillance footage through Clearview AI, which returned a false match. Detectives did not corroborate it, such as by checking his location, and omitted the tool from the arrest affidavit, so it could not be contested. A second jurisdiction reused the identification for another warrant.

sector.quote: Critically, no supporting evidence was developed to corroborate the identification

technology.quote: appears to be the result of a cascade of technologies — beginning with a bad facial recognition match

severity.quote: who was wrongly jailed for nearly a week after being misidentified by facial recognition technology

notes: Racial bias in the match is suggested by a French report but not shown for this case.

summary: Two Australian newspapers removed an opinion article after finding it had been prepared with Microsoft Copilot without the editors being told. The author said she used the tool only to structure her own notes.
technical_summary: An academic used Microsoft Copilot to turn notes into a structured opinion piece and submitted it without disclosing AI assistance. Peers noticed stylistic patterns typical of AI text. The publisher's standards on AI use were not met, exposing mismatched norms on AI disclosure between institutions.

sector.quote: The opinion piece was itself written with AI.

failure_mode.quote: The incident exposes the differing norms in the use of AI between institutions and industries.

notes: Dispute is over undisclosed AI assistance, not factual errors.

summary: A fake image appearing to show the US Vice President arguing with his wife in a restaurant spread on Facebook and X. Its creator later confirmed it was made with ChatGPT, and the Vice President mocked the rumor.
technical_summary: An image generated with ChatGPT, originally made as a video thumbnail, was reposted stripped of context and presented as an authentic photo. AI-detection tools gave mixed results, while the creator's confirmation settled its origin.

summary: A 77-year-old woman in Scotland lost about 17,000 pounds to a romance scam in which scammers used AI-generated videos, images and documents to pose as a woman she believed she was in a relationship with.
technical_summary: Scammers used generative AI to produce recorded video messages and supporting documents for a fictitious persona, replacing live video calls that were refused. The synthetic media built trust, which was used to extract gift card purchases and bank transfers until a bank flagged fraud.

summary: A lawsuit alleges an AI meeting assistant recorded and analyzed the voice of an Illinois resident in a virtual meeting, built a voice profile and attributed statements to her, though she had no account and gave no written consent.
technical_summary: A meeting transcription assistant with speaker-recognition features reportedly creates and retains voiceprints of all participants, including non-users who never accepted its terms. The complaint alleges no notice, written consent or published retention policy, in breach of Illinois biometric privacy law. Allegations are unproven.

summary: A Massachusetts police officer allegedly used a license-plate reader system and other police databases to track a former partner who said she had fled an abusive relationship. The department found repeated improper searches and ended its contract with the vendor.
technical_summary: An automated license plate reader network and other law-enforcement databases were queried by an insider with legitimate access, for personal purposes rather than any investigation. Access controls and audit review did not prevent repeated searches over about two years before the woman found them herself.

summary: Researchers asked Microsoft Copilot common medical questions about frequently prescribed drugs and found only about half its answers matched scientific consensus. They judged many answers could cause serious harm, and some could cause death.
technical_summary: A study of 500 Copilot answers on the most popular drug questions scored accuracy and completeness. Only 54% agreed with scientific consensus, and reviewers rated a large share as potentially harmful. The failure is unreliable generated medical advice presented to lay users, with no realized harm reported.

sector.quote: Researchers based in Germany and Belgium recently asked Microsoft Copilot a range of commonly asked medical questions.

notes: Risk estimate from a research evaluation, not from reported patient injuries.

summary: Google search showed a featured answer claiming no African country starts with the letter K. The text came from a chatbot-written post that Google's systems picked up and repeated, and its AI search feature repeated it too.
technical_summary: Google's snippet extraction scraped a ChatGPT-generated, nonsensical answer posted on a forum and presented it as fact. The experimental generative search feature paraphrased the same false claim and gave wrong answers to similar queries, showing weak filtering of AI-generated web content.

summary: Security researchers found that the AI web-app builder Lovable could be jailbroken to produce and host convincing phishing pages and tools to track stolen data, letting beginners set up scams in minutes.
technical_summary: Prompting techniques bypassed Lovable's safeguards so the LLM-based platform generated lookalike credential-harvesting pages, evasion methods and admin dashboards, and hosted them live. The finding comes from a benchmark of AI agents' resistance to misuse, with little pushback from the platform.

failure_mode.quote: has been found to be the most susceptible to jailbreak attacks
allowing novice and aspiring cybercrooks to set up lookalike credential harvesting pages

notes: Documented by researcher testing; no specific victims reported.

summary: After England lost the Euro 2020 final, trolls posted racist comments and emojis at three Black players on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter. The platforms did not proactively catch many of them and relied on user reports.
technical_summary: Automated moderation on the platforms did not detect emoji-based and other racist abuse aimed at the players' accounts. Facebook said it does not proactively moderate such emoji attacks and relies on user reports, so removals came after users flagged the content.
